rv.q: Played as a caper, “The BFG” makes for a pleasant evening of family entertainment — but on the page, it was something more.
Audiences will have enough fun but, while intermittently showing the RSC’s artistic power, this sadly doesn’t feel like the giant hit its finances need.
This is a big, friendly triumph.
This new staging is a joyful, uplifting theatrical experience and even the hardest-hearted cynic may find themselves brushing away a sneaky tear by the end.
The Royal Shakespeare Company’s new production of The BFG defines it.
The BFG is a splendiferous triumph of imagination, a theatrical treat for audiences of all ages.

cn.t: The RSC's adaptation of Roald Dahl's beloved tale enchants critics with its theatrical magic, heart, and creative ingenuity. Reviewers praise the production's dazzling stagecraft and faithful capture of Dahl's signature humor and wonder.
